title: Pace Gallery celebrates Constantin Brancusi's 150th anniversary with London exhibition
summary: In celebration of the 150th anniversary of the birth of Constantin Brancusi, presents Matrix Muse , its first solo exhibition of the artist’s work since announcing representation of the estate, at its gallery in London from November 25, 2026, through January 30, 2027. Featuring never-before-exhibited drawings and archival materials alongside four major sculptures, Matrix Muse traces Brancusi’s fascination with metaphysical origins, which continually inspired his quest to create an unprecedented art form. The exhibition is curated by Dr. Jérôme Neutres, an independent curator, former president of the Musée du Luxembourg in Paris, and longtime member of the board of directors of the Réunion des Musées nationaux-Grand palais of France, who was named an Officer of the Order of Arts and Letters by the French Ministry of Culture in 2023. title: Over fifty artists explore space, body, and perception at Kunstmuseum Basel
summary: The exhibition When I’m Here at the Kunstmuseum Basel | Gegenwart gathers works from between 1970 and 2026 by over fifty artists, almost half of whom live in Basel. The works on view are drawn from three major collections in Basel—the Öffentliche Kunstsammlung Basel (the public art collection of Basel), the Emanuel Hoffmann Foundation, and the collection of Kunstkredit Basel-Stadt—and reflect a wide range of approaches to art-making. The exhibition title is drawn from a work by Rémy Zaugg: “And would the world look at me when I’m here”—the words with which a painting from 1995/98 addresses the viewer. A work of art has a history of its own, but each encounter with it takes place in the here and now: and while the artwork may appear to remain unchanged, times change, as do the people who look at it and the contexts in which they see it. title: The Vancouver Art Gallery continues to build its collection for future generations with nearly 200 new acquisitions
summary: The Vancouver Art Gallery announced nearly 200 new acquisitions made through purchases and generous donations in 2026, growing its permanent collection to over 14,000 works. Together, these additions strengthen the Gallery?s holdings of major international artists, expand representation of historically underrepresented voices and preserve important artistic histories from British Columbia and beyond. Among the notable acquisitions are Molt (Los Angeles-Chicago-Woodridge-New York-Vancouver-) (2022?26), a major new installation created specifically for the Gallery by Canadian artist and 2026 Sobey Art Award winner Lotus L. Kang; Tokerman (2026), a significant new painting by internationally recognized Vancouver?based artist and recipient of the 2026 Audain Prize, Steven Shearer, currently on display in Highlights from the Collection; and Future Geography: Tarantula Nebula (2024) by renowned Brazilian artist Clarissa Tossin, whose

title: German Photobook Prize announces 2026 winners with ten gold medals awarded
summary: The German Photobook Prize (Deutscher Fotobuchpreis) has announced its 2026 winners, awarding ten gold medals alongside numerous silver and bronze distinctions to publications that demonstrate the extraordinary diversity and vitality of contemporary photographic publishing. Organized annually by the International Festival of Photographic Images in Regensburg, the competition attracted 370 submissions from publishers, institutions, photographers and independent artists across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. A total of 87 photobooks were nominated and presented at the Frankfurt Book Fair in October, followed by the Stuttgart Book Weeks, before the awards ceremony took place in Regensburg on November 21, 2026. The award-winning publications will now embark on a yearlong international tour through Germany, Europe and Asia. title: Lisa Marei Schmidt appointed new Director of Kunstmuseum Bern and Zentrum Paul Klee
summary: The Board of Trustees of the Umbrella Foundation Kunstmuseum Bern / Zentrum Paul Klee has appointed Lisa Marei Schmidt as the new director of Kunstmuseum Bern and Zentrum Paul Klee, as well as chair of the Management Board. The two institutions are among the most important art institutions in Switzerland, and have distinct profiles which Schmidt aims to strengthen and take further during the next phase of development. A German art historian, she has been director of the Brücke-Museum in Berlin since 2017. In 2023, the museum was awarded "Museum of the Year" by The German Association of Art Critics (AICA). Through her professional expertise, her leadership skills, and her open understanding of the role of museums with an emphasis on art education and social participation, Schmidt distinguished herself throughout the international multi-stage recruitment process. title: Piguet unveils the previously unseen Carleton Smith collection
summary: Alongside the masterpieces from the Baron de Reuter & Gordon Bennett collection, Piguet will present a significant selection of modern and contemporary art on Wednesday, 9 December at 6 pm. Highlights include a sculpture by Henry Moore created for the prestigious Pritzker Architecture Prize, as well as previously unseen works by Marc Chagall and Jack Butler Yeats, acquired directly from the artists and held ever since by the family of arts patron Carleton Smith. Two major paintings by Antoni T?pies and Manolo Vald?s complete this exceptional selection, allowing Piguet to once again celebrate the great masters of Spanish painting. An American professor, musicologist, journalist and prominent patron of the arts, Carleton Smith (1908?1984) was an influential figure in the international cultural world. title: National Gallery of Canada celebrates Takao Tanabe's centenary with major retrospective
summary: The National Gallery of Canada presents Takao Tanabe: Inside Passage, a major retrospective celebrating one of Canada?s most influential artists, who turned 100 on September 16, 2026. On view until April 18, 2027, the exhibition brings together more than 50 paintings from private, corporate, and public collections, spanning seven decades of artistic achievement. It offers an unprecedented opportunity to explore the remarkable breadth, depth, and innovation of Tanabe?s prolific practice. Following its acclaimed debut at the Audain Art Museum in Whistler, British Columbia, Takao Tanabe Inside Passage is now presented at the NGC before travelling to the Art Gallery of Greater Victoria in the spring of 2027. The exhibition and accompanying catalogue are co-produced by the three institutions. The exhibition will also travel to the Mackenzie Art Gallery, Regina, at a date that will soon be confirmed.

title: Rare European collection of six pre-war Packards heads to Osenat auction in Paris
summary: This magnificent collection, unique in Europe, of six pre-war Packards is truly breathtaking in the elegance of the cars and their show condition inside and out. They date from 1917 to 1931 and are estimated to sell for ?500,000 to ?700,000 at Osenat Auctions in Paris on December 14. At the dawn of the 1930s, Packard stood for excellence in American motoring. Known for its build quality, distinguished engines and refined coachwork, the Detroit marque catered to exacting customers who valued both distinction and perfection. The question the collection poses is why would a French collector be inspired to collect this American marque? One glance will tell you, the elegance, design flair and sheer brio of these cars bring out an itch to own them in anyone with a passion for cars. The man who brought these cars together and looked after them so lovingly was a French businessman and collector who has since passed away. His heirs are now offering it at auction. title: Sara Berman's new paintings summon a cast of masked fairground and folklore characters
summary: Sara Berman's Dress Rehearsal is now open at Patricia Low Contemporary, Venice A London-based artist, Sara Berman began her career in fashion, studying at Central Saint Martins before founding and running her own fashion label for 15 years. After a successful career as a designer, she returned to education to study painting at the Slade School of Fine Art, completing her MFA in 2016. Her experience in fashion continues to inform her artistic practice, particularly her interest in clothing, the body, materiality and the ways in which we construct and communicate identity. In Dress Rehearsal, this relationship between clothing and identity takes on a distinctly theatrical dimension. Bringing together a cast of characters drawn from folklore, the fairground and the stage, the exhibition explores the process of becoming someone else through costume and performance. title: Robbie Bushe elected as President of the Royal Scottish Academy
summary: At an Assembly of Academicians, Robbie Bushe was elected President of the Royal Scottish Academy, succeeding Gareth Fisher PPRSA, who has led the Academy through its bicentenary year. Elected to the Academy in 2017, Bushe has played an active role in its work over a number of years, previously serving as Secretary from 2018 to 2021 and more recently as Chair of the Exhibitions and Events Committee from 2022 to 2025. His connection to the Academy is also a longstanding family one, with his father, sculptor Fred Bushe, having also been an Academician. His appointment follows a landmark year for the RSA, with its 200th anniversary celebrated through an expansive programme of exhibitions, events and activity across Scotland and beyond. As an independent, membership-led organisation, the Royal Scottish Academy is governed by its 121 Academicians, who are preeminent in the disciplines of art and architecture. title: Paula do Prado maps connections across the Southern Hemisphere in new exhibition
summary: The Art Gallery of New South Wales presents The Star Net Holds the Summer, an expansive new installation by artist Paula do Prado. Co-curated and co-commissioned with Artspace, the exhibition is the latest in the Art Gallery's Contemporary Projects series ? a dedicated platform supporting ambitious new work by Australian artists. Do Prado is a Uruguay-born, Sydney-based artist whose intricate weaving practice connects ancestral knowledge, cultural memory and contemporary experience. Drawing on her Charr?a, Iberian and West African Bantu heritage, do Prado creates vibrant textile works that explore relationships between body, land and spirit. Her work is underpinned by the notion of sentipensar (feel?thinking), meaning ?to use both mind and heart? and is grounded in Indigenous philosophies associated with Abya Yala, a Guna-language term for the Americas. title: Amos Rex: Art and technology at the centre of Amos Rex's 2027 spring and summer programme
summary: In 2027, three international artists bring their visions of the future to Amos Rex. Laure Prouvost fills the museum?s largest hall with an immersive installation that takes the audience into the world of quantum technologies. Natasha Tontey explores alternative futures through film and new technology, and in summer, Tai Shani invites the audience to dream. The spring and summer seasons reflect Amos Rex?s ambition to make the Nordic region a meeting point for dynamic thinking about art and technology. In her installation We Felt a Star Dying, Laure Prouvost imagines what reality might feel like at the quantum level. There, all things are interconnected: even the death of a distant star touches us here and now. At its centre is The Beginning, a sculptural video installation in which a circular screen acts like the lens of a telescope or microscope. title: Galerie Miranda presents Nancy Wilson-Pajic: Fashion photograms in cyanotype
summary: In celebration of the major acquisition in 2026 by the Centre Pompidou of works spanning over forty years of Nancy Wilson-Pajic's career, Galerie Miranda is proposing a personal exhibition of unique, emblematic works by the artist: 7 monumental photograms in cyanotype featuring haute couture robes and accessories by designers Christian Lacroix, Christian Dior and Alexander McQueen: "My research from the early 1980s into historical photographic process led me to explore permanent photographic printing processes, with iron salts. Of these processes, which includes platinum, palladium and chrysotype (gold), the cyanotype process provided a simplicity and economy that encouraged experimentation. The photogram (baptized 'Shadogram' by Christian Schad and later 'photogram' by Lazlo Moholy-Nagy or 'Rayogram' by Man Ray) is a photographic print obtained by interposing an object between a photo-sensitive surface and a light source. title: Taipei Fine Arts Museum convenes global thinkers for'Forum on Contemporary Art and Technics'
summary: On November 21 and 22, Taipei Fine Arts Museum (TFAM) held the "Forum on Contemporary Art and Technics." Over two days, artists, critics, scholars, curators and museum professionals from Taiwan and abroad met to ask how technology shapes the knowledge, phenomena and practices of contemporary art. The forum grew out of the museum's ongoing research. Since late 2023, TFAM has published a series of themed issues of its journal Modern Art on advanced technology, war, video games and AI, as well as the anthology Contemporary Texts: Technics. This line of research responds to a period in which the pandemic, recent wars and the spread of AI have changed how art is made and seen. title: Ilmin Museum of Art marks its building's centenary with group exhibition 'MANA'
summary: Ilmin Museum of Art is presenting MANA from Wednesday, November 25, 2026, through Sunday, January 24, 2027, to mark the 100th anniversary of the museum?s building. MANA attends to the diverse forces acting on bodies, machines, and objects through the lens of contemporary art. The exhibition examines how humans exchange force with other beings and reflects on the relationship between the forces that initiate movement and the efforts to sustain it. This examination extends beyond humans to encompass all things that move in response to their surroundings. Through sculpture, installation, and video, the six participating artists?Goyoson, Jisu Kwak, Donghee Koo, Murphy Yum, Hyungkoo Lee, and Geumhyung Jeong?explore how external conditions alter the body, how resistance and equilibrium sustain an object?s form, and how machines and

title: Monroe Gallery of Photography presents major Alfred Eisenstaedt exhibition ahead of 25th anniversary
summary: Monroe Gallery of Photography opened a major exhibition of classic and seldom-seen photographs by Alfred Eisenstaedt. The exhibition continues through January 31, 2027. In 2027, Monroe Gallery of Photograph celebrates its 25th anniversary in Santa Fe. A foundation of Monroe Gallery was meeting ?Eisie?, as he preferred to be called, in New York City in the mid 1980?s. Our relationship with Eisenstaedt inspired our commitment to supporting and preserving the work of photojournalists with the creation of Monroe Gallery. The exhibition of more than 40 photographs features numerous classic images, several little-known gems, and never-before-exhibited photographs that are sure to surprise and intrigue. title: MMCA and Art Institute of Chicago present 'Georgia O'Keeffe and American Modernism'
summary: How does a new artistic language emerge? Georgia O?Keeffe and American Modernism, presented at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea (MMCA), explores how artists in the United States sought new forms of expression in the first half of the twentieth century. Bringing together 117 artworks, the exhibition moves between photography and painting, representation and abstraction, to consider modernism not as the achievement of a single artist, but as a process shaped by artistic exchange, experimentation, and the changing conditions of everyday life. At the center of this story is Alfred Stieglitz (1864?1946), a photographer, publisher, and gallerist who championed photography as a fine art and fostered a community of artists searching for new possibilities. title: Kunsthalle Bega presents Bogdan Ciocodeică's first solo exhibition in Timișoara
summary: Kunsthalle Bega is presenting The Real Me Is the Voice Inside My Head / Eu cel adevărat sunt vocea din capul meu, the first solo exhibition by Romanian architect, designer, and artist Bogdan Ciocodeică, on view in Timișoara through February 27, 2027. What happens when the structures we construct to protect ourselves begin to determine who we become? In The Real Me Is the Voice Inside My Head, Romanian architect, designer, and artist Bogdan Ciocodeică investigates the mechanisms through which identity is concealed, negotiated, and transformed. Bringing together eight works at the intersection of design and sculpture, his first solo exhibition at Kunsthalle Bega examines the fragile boundary between the desire to be seen and the fear of revealing oneself. title: McLaren and RM Sotheby's to auction 2027 Formula 1 car ahead of its public unveiling
summary: McLaren Racing and RM Sotheby’s have once again teamed up to offer the chance to acquire a 2027 McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team car months before the new challenger is unveiled to the public. The successful bidder will become the proud owner of a MCL41 chassis campaigned by one of the team’s F1 drivers; either 2025 World Champion, Lando Norris or Oscar Piastri, during the 2027 FIA Formula 1 World Championship season. The announcement comes after the success of the Triple Crown offering in Abu Dhabi in December 2025, during which the 2026 McLaren MCL40 made auction history when it sold for $11,480,000, becoming the first Formula 1 car to be auctioned before being raced. title: Renata Lucas turns Dortmunder Kunstverein into a playable skatepark and sound installation
summary: How do built environments influence our perception, our behaviour and social interaction? What interactive freedoms does public space provide, what boundaries does it set up, what power structures or configurations of powerlessness are reflected in public space and institutions? The Brazilian artist Renata Lucas addresses herself to these questions by means of conceptual interventions into existing situations, buildings and social spaces. Her works are the result of complex negotiations to open up institutional and public spaces, and of interaction with communities, curators, technicians, municipal offices and other authorities. Conversation of this kind is always a part of Renata Lucas’s working method, in which she adapts things through doing, replans them flexibly as they emerge and determines her scope for artistic intervention. title: Latvian National Museum of Art presents Laimdota Malle's solo exhibition 'Stardust' in Riga
summary: Stardust, a solo exhibition of Laimdota Malle, is on view in the Cupola Hall of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1, Riga) from 28 November 2026 to 21 February 2027. The Stardust exhibition explores potential as a field of possibilities and transformations in which forms emerge, change and disappear. Conceived as a multipart system, the exposition brings together materials, bodies and structures in a state of constant transformation. Abundant growth and gradual decay, control and vulnerability, chaos and self-organisation coexist within it. In this environment, potential reveals itself through temporary configurations. Matter briefly organises itself into a particular form, solidifies, only to dissolve and rearrange itself into another. title: TarraWarra Museum of Art announces summer collection exhibition 'Light Weight'
summary: TarraWarra Museum of Art today announces its collection-led summer exhibition, Light Weight. Curated by Dr Emily Cormack, TarraWarra Museum of Art’s Head of Exhibitions and Programs, the show brings together over thirty celebrated artists revealing the transformative power of light. It will be on view at the Museum from 28 November 2026 until 28 February 2027. This playful exhibition explores the materiality and poetry of light, experimenting with light’s metaphorical and symbolic qualities, as well as its material and physical properties. Exploring light’s ability to elucidate and enlighten, make visible and splinter into a colour spectrum, the exhibition conjures poetic, generative and structural aspects of light, bridging the worlds of poetry and physics and informing how we perceive and exist in the world. title: 13th SITE SANTA FE International Biennial presents artists, title, curatorial vision
summary: SITE SANTA FE announces the 13th SITE SANTA FE International Biennial: There Are Other Worlds, opening June 25, 2027. Curated by Ekow Eshun, the exhibition brings together over 40 artists, including newly commissioned works by Edgar Arceneaux, Firelei Báez, Raven Chacon, Lotus L. Kang, Cauleen Smith, and many others. Working across installation, sculpture, painting, moving image, performance, sound, and other media, the artists explore how art might resist narrowing visions of the future and, instead, offer space for alternative ways of seeing and imagining. title: The Long Welcome: Theme for Bukhara Biennial 2027 and first artists confirmed
summary: The Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation (ACDF) announces The Long Welcome as the theme of the 2027 Bukhara Biennial, with first artists confirmed: Anish Kapoor (India / UK), Koo Jeong A (South Korea), Sevara Haydarova Donazzan (Uzbekistan), Susan Philipsz (UK / Germany), Nigina Mirzadzhanova (Uzbekistan), Precious Okoyomon (Nigeria / USA), Ugo Rondinone (Switzerland), Vivian Suter (Argentina / Switzerland / Guatemala), Joseph Arzoumanov (France / Armenia), Oscar Tuazon (USA), Maksim Vardanyan and Daima Rakhmanbekova (Uzbekistan), Huma Bhabha (Pakistan / USA) and Bethan Laura Wood (UK). Under Artistic Director Kulapat Yantrasast, WHY founder, The Long Welcome brings artists from Uzbekistan and around the world to create new work in dialogue with the city’s people, knowledge and traditions.
